# Platform Overview

Covers dimensions 1 (What It Is), 2 (Licensing), and 12 (Community and
Maturity) of the Temporal evaluation.

## What Temporal Is

Temporal is a durable execution platform that enables developers to build
scalable applications without sacrificing productivity or reliability [1].
The platform automatically handles intermittent failures and retries failed
operations [1].

### Architecture

Temporal uses an event-sourcing model where deterministic Workflow code
orchestrates non-deterministic Activity code [30]. The server is written in
Go (99.5% of the codebase) [1] and consists of four core services:

| Service | Role |
|---------|------|
| Frontend | Stateless gateway exposing gRPC API on port 7233 [23] |
| History | Manages workflow state via event sourcing; most memory-intensive [26] |
| Matching | Routes tasks to workers via Task Queues [10] |
| Worker | Internal system workflows (archival, replication) [10] |

Workers (user-deployed) connect to the Frontend Service via gRPC and poll
Task Queues for work [23]. Workflow code must be deterministic — no threading,
no randomness, no external calls, no network IO, no global state mutation [30].
All non-deterministic operations (API calls, shell commands, database queries)
execute as Activities [30].

### Origin

Temporal was founded by the creators of Uber's Cadence workflow engine. The
GitHub repository originated as a fork of Cadence [1]. The company was
incorporated as Temporal Technologies.

### Supported SDKs

Seven official SDKs: Go, Java, Python, TypeScript, .NET, PHP, Ruby [19].
The Python SDK supports async, threaded, and multiprocess activity execution
modes [19].

## Licensing

| Component | License | Source |
|-----------|---------|--------|
| Temporal Server | MIT | [1] |
| Go SDK | MIT | [1] |
| Python SDK | MIT | [19] |
| TypeScript SDK | MIT | [1] |
| Java SDK | Apache 2.0 | [1] |

The MIT license is OSI-approved and imposes no restrictions on personal,
commercial, or enterprise use [1]. The server source code is fully open —
self-hosting is free with no feature gates or artificial limitations.

Temporal Cloud is a separate paid service ($100/month minimum) [8] but is
not required — all server features are available in the open-source
self-hosted version.

**Personal use implications:** No restrictions. MIT license permits
unrestricted use, modification, and distribution.

### Project Age

Temporal Technologies was founded in 2019, building on the Cadence project
from Uber (which predates Temporal by ~2 years) [1]. The combined lineage
gives Temporal approximately 7+ years of development history.

### Notable Adopters

Production users include OpenAI (Codex agent orchestration), Replit (Agent 3),
Netflix, Stripe, Coinbase, Instacart, and Snap [37][20]. OpenAI uses Temporal
to orchestrate their Codex AI coding agent, and Replit migrated Agent 3 to
Temporal for improved reliability [37][20].

### Release Cadence

160 releases across the project's history [1], averaging roughly 2 releases
per month. The latest release v1.30.3 was published April 1, 2026 [1],
indicating active maintenance.

### Industry Positioning

Temporal joined the Agentic AI Foundation as a Gold Member in December 2025
[34], signaling a strategic pivot toward AI agent orchestration alongside
its core workflow platform positioning.
